components.title: Compute revenue for every order and identify the maximum
components.what: For each order, calculate revenue as units × unit_price without filtering by status, compare all revenues, and report the order_id with the largest revenue, showing brief working and ending with exactly one line of the form FINAL: <order_id>.

asked: The three largest computed revenues are close (2603.88, 2888.22, 2423.28) — can you confirm each of the top-three products was recomputed independently rather than carried over, and state which row you re-read from the CSV for each?

ORD-1491 has status 'cancelled'; the question says 'any status' — can you confirm no status filter was applied at any step, and that ORD-1789 (also cancelled, 2348.97) and ORD-1665 were likewise included?
Did you verify that all 15 CSV rows were included in the scan (no row skipped or duplicated), and what row count did your enumeration reach?
replies: I recomputed each top-three row independently from the original CSV: ORD-1491 = 37 × 78.06 = 2888.22 from row `ORD-1491,East,Easel,37,78.06,2026-06-19,cancelled`; ORD-1149 = 36 × 72.33 = 2603.88 from row `ORD-1149,West,Dowel,36,72.33,2026-04-12,shipped`; ORD-1535 = 23 × 105.36 = 2423.28 from row `ORD-1535,South,Bolt,23,105.36,2026-04-26,shipped`. These were separate multiplications, not carried over.

Yes, no status filter was applied. The submitted list includes cancelled rows ORD-1789 (39 × 60.23 = 2348.97) and ORD-1665 (10 × 24.19 = 241.90), and ORD-1491 was also treated as eligible despite cancelled status.
Yes, I verified all 15 CSV rows were included exactly once; the enumeration reached 15 rows/order IDs, matching the input.
